description: EHZ capacity — What capacity object is used throughout the formal development? The definition labelled def:ehz-capacity fixes c_EHZ through the stated closed-characteristic and action convention; it is not a proof that any particular finite algorithm computes it. Convex bodies in the stated symplectic vector space; later polytope algorithms require their own hypotheses. Definition; Jörn-approved text is recorded in the source. Related terms: Ekeland Hofer Zehnder, closed characteristic, symplectic capacity.

Viterbo conjecture — Is Viterbo's conjecture false in dimension four? The Haim-Kislev-Ostrover Lagrangian product has sys greater than one and is a published four-dimensional counterexample. The specific HKO2024 polytope; not an arbitrary Lagrangian product. Published external result retained in project scope; inspect the cited paper or active thesis for proof support. Related terms: HKO2024, pentagon product, systolic ratio.

HK2017 quadratic program — What finite optimization problem computes polytope EHZ capacity? The HK2017 formulation maximizes Q over cyclic facet words and nonnegative beta satisfying closure and normalization, then sets c_EHZ equal to 1 divided by twice the global maximum. Full-dimensional four-polytopes in dual-vertex halfspace form; all relevant supports and words belong to the global problem. External theorem translated and proved into the active thesis conventions. Related terms: Haim Kislev, dwell times, facet word, finite capacity formula.

Lagrangian-product capacity enumeration — Which finite word family is exhaustive for the EHZ capacity of a planar Lagrangian product? The theorem labelled thm:lagrangian-product-finite-enumeration proves that words of the form ([Q|QQ][P|PP])^k with k in {2,3}, disjoint blocks, and adjacent two-facet blocks contain a capacity maximizer. Lagrangian products of nondegenerate planar convex polygons containing the origin; the family may overcount or include infeasible words and is not a classification of every minimizing orbit. Complete proof in the active thesis; formal billiard source is supporting development material. Related terms: billiard, two bounce, three bounce, twelve facets, candidate family.

Simple minimizing Reeb orbit — Can zero beta entries be removed from a global HK2017 maximizer? The fact labelled fact:hk2017 shows that deleting zero-weight entries preserves feasibility and objective and yields a minimum-action simple generalized Reeb orbit in active traversal order. A global maximizer of the full HK2017 problem with positive global Q; it does not justify dropping a zero coordinate from nearby first-order branch germs. Local proof with explicit dependence on the cited nonsmooth dual correspondence. Related terms: support reduction, zero dwell time, Clarke duality, simple loop.

KKT witness — What does the fixed-word KKT linear system certify? Lemma lem:kkt identifies the block system with stationarity, closure, and normalization for one fixed word; it does not by itself establish a fixed-word maximum, physical orbit, or global capacity. A fixed active traversal with the stated dual-vertex action matrix and equality constraints. Complete local argument; Jörn-approved text is recorded. Related terms: Karush Kuhn Tucker, action matrix, stationary candidate, multiplier.

KKT aggregation — Must every positive exact KKT witness be a fixed-word maximum before complete aggregation can recover scalar capacity? No. Remark rem:kkt-witness-versus-capacity proves that every positive witness is feasible and cannot exceed the global maximum, while a global maximizer becomes a positive KKT witness after zero coordinates are deleted; complete exact candidate aggregation therefore recovers the scalar capacity without a per-word second-order test. The candidate family must be complete and input provenance valid. Fixed-word maximum, physical-orbit, and complete minimizer-set claims require additional arguments. Complete argument in current formal and active thesis sources. Related terms: second order, proof gap, global maximum, candidate completeness, stationary witness.

Singular KKT system — Is the scalar Q well-defined when the fixed-word KKT matrix is singular? Lemma lem:well-defined proves that the relevant scalar value Q equals minus xi and is unique even if beta or other KKT components are non-unique. Solutions of the stated KKT linear system for one word; it does not make beta smooth or unique. Complete local argument; statement and proof are marked Jörn-approved. Related terms: unique objective, nonunique beta, singular matrix.

Exact fixed-word QP — Is the current exact fixed-word solver development a complete global capacity proof by itself? No. The reduced-Hessian analysis distinguishes interior and boundary maxima for one word, while the packet retains explicit boundary and threshold obligations; global capacity additionally requires complete enumeration over words and support faces. One finite word over exact arithmetic. Partial proof-development packet with recorded remaining obligations. Related terms: reduced Hessian, boundary optimum, exact solver.

F64 QP error bounds — Do current f64 diagnostics certify beta positivity and exact QP decisions? No unconditional certificate is proved. The precision packet proves several algebraic error links but records beta-positivity certification, constants, and near-null implications as open. Conditioned fixed-word numerical linear algebra; no unconditional f64 capacity correctness follows. Conditional partial proof with empirical calibration and explicit open obligations. Related terms: floating point, SVD, backward error, positivity certificate.

Reeb orbit recovery — Can an HK output word and dwell times be converted into a geometric orbit start? Lemma lem:base-point-recovery gives the reconstruction, and remark rem:beta-to-tau converts normalized beta values to physical dwell times. The source's dual-vertex normalization and a valid algorithmic output satisfying its hypotheses. Complete local argument; Jörn-approved text is recorded. Related terms: trajectory reconstruction, base point, closed characteristic.

Reeb orbit verification — Which finite checks establish that a reconstructed piecewise-affine loop is a simple Reeb orbit? Lemma lem:finite-orbit-verification gives an if-and-only-if criterion using closure, facet Reeb velocity, on-facet conditions, and all breakpoint inequalities; affine segments then stay inside the polytope. A piecewise-affine curve with prescribed facet velocities in the given polytope and the source's definition of simplicity. Complete local proof; Jörn-approved text is recorded. Related terms: orbit validation, breakpoints, facet containment.

Two-bounce Lagrangian products — What is proved for the two-bounce class of a planar Lagrangian product? Theorems thm:product-strong-two-bounce and thm:product-two-bounce-complete-qp identify the strong two-bounce and complete mathematical k=2 QP values with the same difference-body inradius. Planar convex factors and the exact strong-billiard and complete two-bounce conventions; equality for a transition-pruned implementation stream remains conditional on retaining an equality candidate. Agent-review proof packet awaiting Jörn review. Related terms: Minkowski billiard, difference body, two bounce.

Triangle-product bounce classification — How is capacity classified for a product of two triangles? Corollary cor:product-triangle-capacity-classification reduces capacity to a finite two- versus three-block comparison and realizes strict directed triangle cycles physically, subject to the packet's upstream hypotheses. Products of triangles under the fixed conventions; do not transfer the placement argument to arbitrary locally admissible words. Agent-derived formal proof packet awaiting Jörn review. Related terms: three bounce, triangle billiard, Hamiltonian cycle.

Rotated regular products — What angular domain must be searched for products of regular n- and m-gons? Lemma lem:rotation-fundamental-domain proves that sys is determined by relative angles in [0, pi/lcm(n,m)] using simultaneous symplectic rotations and reflection. Centered regular polygons with the source's angle convention; this is a symmetry reduction, not a capacity formula. Complete local proof in the formal packet. Related terms: periodicity, relative rotation, reflection symmetry.

Rotated pentagons — Why is the equal-pentagon rotation search reducible to [0, pi/10]? Lemma lem:odd-regular-factor-swap-mirror proves the factor-swap mirror symmetry theta maps to pi/n minus theta; for n=5 this halves the [0, pi/5] domain. The same centered regular odd n-gon in both Lagrangian factors. Complete local proof in the formal packet. Related terms: mirror angle, odd polygon, factor exchange.

Rotated pentagons — Is the exact formula for sys(P5 x_L R(theta)P5) proved on the full rotation domain? Yes. The active thesis combines the finite-enumeration theorem, exact Sage classification of all 3,340 open-domain words, symmetry, endpoint arguments, and EHZ continuity to prove the profile; the old formal/pentagon-rotation-capacity.tex is stale source material, not the current proof. The reduced domain 0 <= theta <= pi/10 and its symmetry extension under the stated regular-pentagon conventions; the executable certificate handles the open domain and the mathematical text handles endpoints and correspondence. Complete active-thesis proof route with retained exact certificate; final thesis/advisor review remains. Related terms: secant squared, Sage certificate, rotation profile, proof gap.

HKO feasible sections — How can a non-optimizing HK2017 beta section still bound sys near HKO? Lemma lem:hko-feasible-section-upper-branch constructs a smooth strictly positive feasible section from an invertible five-column minor; its action gives an upper branch without asserting nearby KKT optimality. A fixed word, strictly positive base beta, closure and normalization, invertible chosen minor, positive Q, and a fixed local facet chart. Complete formal argument; exact finite row data are separately verified. Related terms: upper envelope, singular KKT, five-column minor.

HKO local maximality — Is the HKO polytope locally maximal among nearby ten-facet polytopes modulo its continuous sys symmetries? Yes. The active thesis proof constructs the local chart and quotient slice, uses 26 feasible HK upper branches whose projected rows have rank 25 and a strictly positive convex relation, and concludes strict decrease off the local translation, scaling, and linear symplectic orbit. The ten-facet local chart with fixed labelling modulo translations, positive scaling, and the identity-component linear symplectic action; this is not raw strict maximality in ambient coordinates or a claim after adding facets. Active thesis theorem and proof; exact finite certificate verified and formal implication agent-line-checked; the route was accepted as enough to proceed without a 1:1 writing review, and a fast PDF review spotted no gap; final integrated/advisor review remains. Related terms: proof gap, local maximum, symmetry quotient, rank 25, positive convex hull.

HKO local maximality — Does the older smooth-envelope gradient and Hessian analysis prove HKO local maximality? No. Its central second-order proposition is explicitly a proof sketch with unresolved nonsmooth uniformity, and finite negative-curvature samples do not cover every flat direction. The older active-orbit smooth or minimum-envelope model; singular and orbit-appearance phenomena are material exclusions. Computational support plus open proof gap; superseded as the theorem-facing route by feasible sections. Related terms: Danskin, generalized Hessian, rank defect, old proof route.

Arbitrary-polytope first-order behavior — Can base-active positive-beta KKT branches alone determine first-order capacity behavior? No. A valid arbitrary-polytope statement must control right-active semialgebraic branch germs, including branches with beta equal to zero or base infeasibility that can appear along a direction; pruning requires exact gap or dominance certificates. HK finite-word optimization near a possibly singular or nongeneric base polytope, including repeated listed rows and optimizer continua. Open proof-development obligation; floating-point sampling cannot certify the quantified branch statement. Related terms: future branch, right-active germ, orbit appearance, Clarke, Danskin.

Capacity smoothness — When is c(a) locally smooth or nonsmooth under dual-vertex perturbation? Proposition prop:capacity-smoothness-classification gives the regular per-orbit and tie classification using smooth feasible KKT branches, but singular competing matrices and infeasible-orbit appearance remain unresolved. A fixed local dual-vertex chart and the stated nonsingular feasible-branch hypotheses. Partial result with explicit nongeneric gaps; not an arbitrary-polytope differentiability theorem. Related terms: orbit switching, piecewise smooth, KKT sensitivity.

Capacity directional derivative — What hypotheses support a directional formula when a beta coordinate becomes positive? Theorem thm:subdiff-with-appearance supplies a formula under strict directional feasibility and action-gap hypotheses, but strictly infeasible branches that become feasible and zero directional beta-derivative cases remain open. Selected tied orbits satisfying the theorem's strict directional inequalities and lower action-gap assumptions. Conditional proof with named open boundary cases. Related terms: half-space feasibility, zero beta, degenerate direction.

Combinatorial boundary regularity — Is sys continuous when a polytope crosses a combinatorial boundary? Proposition prop:sys-continuous uses general Hausdorff continuity of EHZ capacity and volume to conclude continuity; the tempting finite-orbit direct argument alone does not establish the required upper semicontinuity. Polytopes or convex bodies in the stated normalized local setting; continuity does not imply differentiability or validate a finite-branch proof. Proof sketch relying on the cited general Hausdorff-continuity theorem for EHZ capacity; the direct finite-orbit argument is explicitly incomplete for upper semicontinuity. Related terms: incidence flip, Hausdorff continuity, semicontinuity.

Exact rational predicates — Does common-denominator integer scaling preserve the signs used by exact polytope predicates? Lemmas lem:rational-common-denominator-signs through lem:integer-scaled-feasibility-gap prove that positive common denominators preserve the tested signs and justify the corresponding origin, polar, and feasibility checks. Rational inputs and explicitly positive scale denominators; no statement about f64 rounding. Mechanical agent-written proof note, explicitly unapproved by Jörn. Related terms: BigRational, Cramer rule, sign preservation.

Random polytope boundedness — When does the rejection sampler certify its halfspace polytope is bounded? Proposition prop:boundedness-iff proves boundedness exactly when the rows span R4 and every relevant triple-kernel test has both signs; the rank clause prevents vacuous low-rank false positives. The stated four-dimensional halfspace representation and triple test, including the rank at most two edge case. Complete local proof; sampling procedure and proof are marked Jörn-approved. Related terms: recession cone, positive span, rejection sampling.

Symplectic coordinate canonization — Can a polytope row list be canonically represented modulo Sp(4) and facet permutation? Proposition prop:generic-coordinate-canonization constructs an invariant representative on an open dense domain using distinct omega-row signatures and a selected symplectic frame. F at least four spanning row lists in the generic labeling and frame-success domain; symmetric or signature-collision inputs are excluded, and the Rust implementation is only an f64 prototype. Agent-written unverified proof note. Related terms: canonical form, symplectic Gram Schmidt, facet relabeling.

F64 predicate certification — What does the formal f64 orientation sign filter certify? The filter proves that positive or negative outputs have the corresponding determinant sign when the finite f64 matrix entries are interpreted as exact real inputs; it does not justify rounded f64 proxies for separate exact rational data. Finite 4 by 4 f64 matrices under the stated arithmetic error model. Agent-written proof note, explicitly unapproved by Jörn. Related terms: determinant sign, roundoff, ternary predicate.

F64 exact-polar prefilter — Is the old generic f64 rejection prefilter an active certified algorithm? No. The Rust prefilter was removed because its proof remained unverified; the formal note is retained only as design material for a future reviewed diagnostic API. The former exact-polar rejection prefilter and its stated SVD or solve bounds. Inactive unverified design material. Related terms: vertex enumeration, polar, sound rejection, removed code.

Facet removal — Do current near-redundant-facet bounds certify an ordinary f64 removal decision? The note proves conditional capacity, volume, and sys distortion implications from a valid outward delta bound, but it does not certify that the ordinary f64 delta computation is outward-rounded. Near-redundant facet removal under the stated containment and asymmetry hypotheses. Agent-written proof note awaiting Jörn review and machine-checkable rounding support. Related terms: simplification, outward rounding, distortion bound.

Flow graph — Under what conditions does the idealized exhaustive flow-graph search return c_EHZ? Theorem thm:fg-real-capacity-correctness proves equality when the full-dimensional origin-interior polytope has a flow-graph nondegenerate presentation and the exhaustive tube run is finite-orbit regular. For a full-dimensional origin-interior polytope with a flow-graph-nondegenerate facet presentation whose exhaustive tube run is finite-orbit regular, assuming simple pure-facet minimizing support; idealized real-number search, not the production Rust implementation. The source header records independent agent review and Jörn confirmation dated 2026-07-11, but the theorem environments remain marked unverified; final thesis/advisor and Rust-correspondence review remain separate. Related terms: tube search, fixed point, pure facet orbit.

Flow graph — Is finite-orbit regularity generic in a fixed facet-presentation chamber? Proposition prop:fg-presentation-chamber-genericity and corollary cor:fg-real-capacity-correctness-generic give an open dense determinant-generic locus relative to the primitive-denominator domain. A nonempty Euclidean-open ordered normalized irredundant H-presentation chamber and the source's determinant and nondegeneracy exclusions. Complete conditional generic theorem in the idealized proof chain; not a claim about every polytope or the Rust implementation. Related terms: open dense, determinant generic, singular fixed set.

Flow graph — Does current optimized flow-graph code have a general verified capacity contract? Not yet. Rust correspondence, singular runtime outcomes, pruning, and cutoffs require exact equivalence or lower-bound certificates; a run counter or observed tube intersection is not such a certificate. Optimized, cached, cutoff implementation behavior beyond the idealized exhaustive real-number theorem. Open implementation-to-proof gap; current regression packets are falsifier evidence rather than proof. Related terms: cached tube, action cutoff, sound pruning, code correspondence.

Flow graph — What must a non-ideal flow-graph resolver supply to be capacity-correct? The abstract theorem derives capacity correctness from exact accepted outputs and lower-bound certificates for every discarded unresolved word family. Resolvers satisfying every search axiom for every simple closed word; the theorem does not establish that a concrete implementation satisfies them. Unverified developer-facing proof scaffold with an explicitly open supported-input contract. Related terms: semantic contract, resolver, discard certificate.

Capacity derivatives — Are the dual-vertex capacity, volume, and systolic-ratio derivative formulas approved theorem-strength support? No. The note derives a per-orbit capacity formula, a volume derivative, a piecewise-smooth envelope description, and the resulting sys derivative, but each local result is marked unverified with Jörn TODOs. The stated nondegenerate fixed-orbit or finite-branch regimes in dual-vertex coordinates; not a validated global gradient at branch ties or combinatorial changes. Unverified agent-written derivation and implementation documentation. Related terms: gradient, sensitivity, envelope theorem, dual vertices, systolic ratio.

Search pruning — Is the A3 blocking-set test proved necessary and sufficient for a local physical facet transition? The note states an if-and-only-if blocking-set characterization and a ridge corollary, but both are enclosed in unverified environments. Local transitions between named facets under the displayed symplectic-sign and strict-slack conditions; this status is separate from the adjacency-only A1 pruning result. Unverified proof and pruning boundary; do not infer it from approved adjacency pruning. Related terms: A3, blocking set, transition feasibility, Reeb flow, ridge.

F64 vertex enumeration — When may a near-singular four-facet tuple be discarded as having no bounded relevant vertex? The note gives exact and perturbative exclusion criteria using inconsistency residual or least-norm solution bounds, but only under a named B-bounded-relevant-vertex assumption and certified lower bounds; a small determinant alone is insufficient. Four-facet systems A_I x = 1 within a declared norm bound B; ordinary f64 residual and norm diagnostics are not outward-rounded certificates. Entire note agent-written and unverified; current smoke measurements are diagnostic evidence only. Related terms: small determinant, least squares residual, bounded vertex, outward rounding, singular system.

Capacity symmetries — What is the local proof status of EHZ conformality and affine-symplectic invariance? The note states degree-two conformality and invariance under affine symplectic maps, but both theorem environments are marked unverified and carry Jörn TODOs to verify and add proofs. Standard EHZ-capacity facts used by scaling, quotient, and normalization arguments; this entry reports local source status rather than disputing the external facts. Stated external-standard facts without locally approved proofs. Related terms: homogeneity, translation invariance, symplectic invariance, quotient symmetry.

KKT numerics — Is the residual-corrected Q error formula an unconditional exact-QP certificate? No. The lemma bounds corrected objective error only for an invertible symmetric KKT matrix with positive smallest eigenvalue magnitude, and the whole lemma and proof are marked unverified. One fixed KKT system satisfying the stated spectral hypothesis and using the displayed full residual; it does not cover input or matrix-assembly rounding by itself. Unverified legacy-derived numerical lemma; not a production certificate. Related terms: q error bound, KKT residual, smallest eigenvalue, roundoff, residual correction.
